title: India Firm Favourites as Bangladesh Eye Upset in Women's Asia Cup Semi-Final
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's unbeaten side meet Bangladesh in Dubai on Thursday, chasing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title.
body:
• India face Bangladesh in the first semi-final of the Women's Asia Cup 2026 on Thursday, September 10, at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, starting 8 PM IST.
  • India have won 21 of 24 women's T20 internationals against Bangladesh, including the last eight in a row; Bangladesh's last win came in the 2018 Asia Cup final.
  • Smriti Mandhana is the tournament's leading run-scorer with 152 runs in three innings, while Bangladesh's Marufa Akter has taken seven wickets at an economy of 3.27.
  • The winners meet the victors of Friday's second semi-final between defending champions Sri Lanka and Pakistan in the final on September 13.

India start as firm favourites in a high-stakes semi-final against Bangladesh at the Women's Asia Cup 2026 on Thursday, with a place in the September 13 final — and a shot at a record-extending title — on the line in Dubai.

The first semi-final begins at 8 PM IST at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Harmanpreet Kaur's side topped Group A with an unbeaten run, while Bangladesh finished runners-up in Group B to set up the knockout clash.

The road to the semi-final

India's campaign has been commanding. After comfortable wins over Thailand and Hong Kong, they steamrolled Pakistan by seven wickets in the group-stage marquee clash — a match in which Shafali Verma crossed 3,000 T20I runs. India have won the Asia Cup a record seven times in nine editions, though they arrive as champions of 2022 with defending champions Sri Lanka still in the field.

Bangladesh's route was rockier but resilient. After beating Indonesia and losing to Sri Lanka, they sealed their semi-final berth with a 34-run win over hosts UAE on September 8, with Sharmin Akhter's 38 off 31 balls lifting them past 100. They also hold a psychological card: their victory over Sri Lanka in the group stage, where Sobhana Mostary's 34 anchored the chase.

Key battles

The headline contest is India's batting against Bangladesh's new-ball spearhead. Smriti Mandhana has been the tournament's standout batter, accumulating 152 runs from three innings at an average of 50.66 and a strike rate of 178.82, including a century. Alongside Shafali Verma and captain Harmanpreet Kaur, she anchors a top order with few peers in Asia.

Bangladesh's hopes rest heavily on Marufa Akter. The right-arm seamer has taken seven wickets in three matches — the most for her team and joint-third overall — at a miserly economy rate of 3.27, striking in her opening spell in every game. She dismissed Sri Lankan captain Chamari Athapaththu for 1 during the group stage. Ahead of the biggest match of her career, Marufa made an emotional appeal to supporters in a Bangladesh Cricket Board video.

"Please keep us all in your prayers so that we can finish tomorrow's match on a high note."

— Marufa Akter, Bangladesh pacer

The numbers, though, are daunting for Bangladesh. The head-to-head record in women's T20Is reads 24 matches, 21 wins for India and three for Bangladesh. The Tigresses have not beaten India since that famous three-wicket win in the 2018 Asia Cup final — eight straight defeats have followed.

Conditions and the other semi-final

Dubai has been a balanced venue: across 29 women's T20Is, teams batting first have won 15 and chasing sides 14, with an average first-innings score of 122. Spinners have found assistance in the middle overs, which suits both attacks.

Friday's second semi-final pits defending champions Sri Lanka against Pakistan — a rematch of group-stage intensity — with the final scheduled for Sunday, September 13.

How to watch

In India, the semi-final airs on the Sony Sports Network and streams on SonyLIV. UK viewers can watch on Sony Max, Bangladesh on T Sports, the MENA region on Starzplay, and audiences in Malaysia, Hong Kong, Singapore and continental Europe on Cricbuzz. For the diaspora, the 8 PM IST start translates to a morning watch in the US — 7:30 AM Pacific.
